content: Bisoctrizole, also known by its USAN name and marketed under the brand Tinosorb® M, is a chemical compound used in sunscreens to absorb ultraviolet (UV) radiation. Its chemical name is Methylene Bis-Benzotriazolyl Tetramethylbutylphenol. This compound is a broad-spectrum UV absorber, meaning it effectively absorbs both UVB and UVA rays. Additionally, it has the ability to reflect and scatter UV radiation, enhancing its protective properties. Bisoctrizole is classified as a hybrid UV absorber. It is manufactured in the form of small particles, typically less than 200 nanometers in size, similar to microfine zinc oxide and titanium dioxide. However, unlike these mineral-based compounds, bisoctrizole is organic, aligning it with the majority of active ingredients used in sunscreens. In sunscreen formulations, it is incorporated into the water phase as a 50% suspension, whereas mineral micropigments are generally added to the oil phase. One of the notable characteristics of bisoctrizole is its high photostability, meaning it undergoes minimal photodegradation when exposed to sunlight. This property also allows it to stabilize other UV absorbers in sunscreen formulations, particularly octyl methoxycinnamate (commonly known as octinoxate). Importantly, unlike some other organic sunscreen ingredients, bisoctrizole has been shown to exhibit no estrogenic effects in in vitro studies. While bisoctrizole is not approved for use by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), it has been approved for use in the European Union and various other regions around the world.
